params.body:
Collecting gets its own clock, so it no longer waits for the engine.

This branch builds on #256 (the collect clock in `phase_runs`) and contains its commit; merging this one makes #256 redundant.

Until now collect was one of the engine's phases, chosen when its score won, at most every 30 minutes, and in the same process as everything else. A run of deploys (2 October, nothing in from 16:33 for over an hour) or a long phase meant nothing came in.

- `ops/crontab`: collect runs at :05 and :35, whatever the engine does. It replaces the two-hourly line that only fired when the engine was down. The guard `^(/usr/bin/)?node packages/pipeline/collect.mjs` sees a collect started by cron or by the engine.
- `collect.mjs` marks the clock itself (`collect-started` at start, `collect` at the end), so a run by either counts. With `--if-due=25` it steps aside when the last run is under 25 minutes old or a run started in the last 15 minutes is still going.
- The engine keeps collect as a fallback: it reads the shared clock every loop and calls collect with `--if-due=25`, so it only collects when cron did not.
- `test/phase-clocks.test.mjs` and `test/cron-guards.test.mjs` cover it. 985 tests pass.

After merge the crontab needs `bin/crontab-install --apply` on the box (as for #255).
params.title: Collect has its own clock
